label: <DEL> step when the sequence began with i (about to output i), longer sequences
explanation: 98% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (t == L, so recall_idx 0), and 95% of it falls in sequences whose first original token is i, which is the token about to be output (out_tok i lift 54x). It almost never fires in the copy phase and only weakly in the late original phase (1.7% of mass, at t = 5-8 of i-initial sequences). Firing rate rises with length: L <= 5 is nearly silent and the rate peaks at L = 8-9 (to_go 7-8 lift 6-10x). It does NOT fire on most i-initial delimiter steps (precision ~0.23 with L >= 6). The prefix content partly sets whether it fires: inputs just before <DEL> of t/e/w/u/v/c and a 1, f or t anywhere in the sequence are enriched, but no simple rule separates firing from non-firing cases. The strongest activations come from long i-initial sequences that contain 1 and f near the start. A handful of weak activations show up at <DEL> in sequences starting with h or l.
